requests.note: the one field the court box's heartbeat does not carry: `kind`. It is a HINT, honoured only when the MAC is unknown — a board cannot re-kind a row that already exists. Absent or "court_box" is today's behaviour exactly; anything else is 400 kind_unknown.

the diagnostic counter a board with one LED and no screen has nowhere else to put. `no_push` is how many heartbeats the board could not push — a body that did not fit its buffer, arrived incomplete, or failed its read on an otherwise-200 response — plus its watchdog-arm failures. It is a SINCE-BOOT TOTAL and is never reset by the server acknowledging it: the board has no way to know which report the server kept, so a counter reset on send would lose the whole count on any lost response. Read a rise between two heartbeats, not the absolute value. Optional and additive: a board that sends nothing is a board reporting zero, which is why it is not in the vector above. The server LOGS it against the device code and stores nothing (a column would be an EF migration for a diagnostic), and it never changes the response: a counter must not be able to take a door out of service.

`events_lost` joins `no_push` as the second diagnostic counter: how many queued events the board's ring overwrote before they could be uploaded. Both are SINCE-BOOT TOTALS, both are omitted at zero, and both SATURATE rather than wrap — the firmware stops at INT32_MAX (2147483647), which is the value here, so a board that has been losing events for a decade reports a ceiling rather than a small number. The server binds both as 64-bit so a saturated or over-large value is still a clean 200; see gate-heartbeat-request-counters-out-of-range. Omitted at zero is why the vector above carries only one of them.

the counters at values no honest board emits, pinned because the answer must be a clean 200 anyway. `no_push` here is INT32_MAX + 1, which an `int?` binding rejects with a 400 for the WHOLE heartbeat — the roster included — so a diagnostic field would have taken the door out of service, which is exactly what the vector above says it must never do. `events_lost` here is negative, which is not a counter at all. Both are IGNORED: not logged as counts, not stored, and not refused. The binding is 64-bit for this reason, not because any board sends these.

a scan the gate could not answer from its roster, or chose not to. Same three fields as /device/activate minus `court` — a door is not on a court, and the row's gate_key is the server's business, not the board's.

an open the gate decided from its own roster while offline. `court` is -1 because there is no relay bank to index; `duration_ms` is how long the lock was released. The API already knows about online opens, so this kind is queued for offline ones only.

`boot_id` IS THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY'S MISSING THIRD FIELD, and it is here because (device, seq) was not one. The ring is RAM-only, so no event survives a reboot, and `seq` resumes from a checkpoint in flash — one record, written in blocks of 64. Erase or tear that record and the board renumbers from 1, against a PERMANENT unique index on the server: every event of the next evening is silently receipted as a duplicate and discarded, INCLUDING the `boot` event the firmware queues precisely so that an operator can see a board restarted. Two boards accidentally sharing a MAC dedup each other the same way. `boot_id` is a per-boot random 32-bit value — `esp_random()` on the board, seedable in the simulator — so the key is (device, boot_id, seq): a renumbered board collides with nothing, and a genuine retry of the same event still carries the same three fields and is still deduplicated. It is a NUMBER, up to 4294967295, which is why the server binds it as 64-bit. `accepted_through` is unchanged: the board holds one boot's events at a time, so the highest seq in the batch means what it always meant.

THE COMPATIBILITY SHAPE, and the reason `boot_id` could be added without a flag day. A body that omits it means boot_id 0 on the server, which is exactly the behaviour (device, seq) always had: every such board shares one boot identity and dedups against itself as before. That covers the COURT BOX, whose renderer omits the field today, and every gate image flashed before this change. The field is additive and optional on the wire and REQUIRED in practice on a gate — the gate's renderer always sets it, and this vector exists so the server's tolerance of its absence is pinned rather than assumed. A subject of `"` is in here too: the bytes come off a QR code and the renderer escapes them, so the corpus carries an escaped one rather than leaving that to a reviewer's imagination.

gate 2.0.0 on a quiet beat. The 1.x fields, then fw_state, net_ver and net_src, then caps LAST. `caps` names every v3 capability the image has; the server keys every new response field on it, so a 1.x gate is answered exactly as before.

the first beat after a POWER-ON reset that found the server down: `restore` says what the board ran on meanwhile — cold (its flash roster, trusted for power_restore_trust_minutes from boot because the outage length is unknowable), warm (an RTC-dated roster after a watchdog or panic reset), or none. Sent on the first accepted beat of a boot only; the server records it on the board's activity.
2.0.1 failed probation; the gate is back on 2.0.0 in its other app slot and will never take 2.0.1 again.

responses.note: `roster` is present and empty rather than absent. The firmware replaces its cache wholesale on every push, so an omitted key would leave a stale roster live — a cancelled booking is expressed by its absence from the NEXT push.

a gate nobody has named yet — auto-registration leaves gate_key null and an admin sets it. The key is still PRESENT on the wire as null: a firmware that reads an absent key as an empty string and a null one as an error would diverge here. It is also the UNNAMED half of the named/unnamed pair: an unnamed gate's roster is ALWAYS empty, whatever the club has booked, so the offline fallback does not start until an admin has named the door. Online scans work from the first heartbeat. Pair this with gate-heartbeat-response-roster-single, which is the named half and is the only shape that may carry entries.

one rostered booking, 30 minutes from its early-entry window opening and 90 minutes from its slot ending. Same TOKEN|relay|opens_in|closes_in grammar as the court box so devlink::parseRosterElement and roster::Roster are reused unchanged; the relay field is always 0. The NAMED half of the pair above: gate_key is set, so this board is allowed a roster at all. A non-empty roster beside a null gate_key is a body the server does not emit.

opens_in is SIGNED and goes negative once the early-entry window is open — this member may already come in. A firmware that parsed it unsigned would read -900 as an enormous positive wait and lock out somebody whose court starts in five minutes.

GateRosterMaxEntries = 48 is a CONTRACT CONSTANT, not a tenant setting: it bounds Roster<48> on the board and, through it, the 4608-byte static response buffer the gate has to hold this in. max_bytes is the budget for the WHOLE body, not the roster alone, and every field in this vector is at the widest the server can emit — a 64-character slug and gate key, the long device_code auto-registration falls back to, and six-digit relative seconds. A budget pinned by a comfortable vector is not pinned.
unlock_seconds is what goes on the lock's release timer — the tenant's gate_unlock_seconds clamped to [1, 30]. Never 0 on an open: a zero-second release is a door that clicks and stays shut.

unknown, expired, or another club's code — one reason for all three on purpose, because telling them apart at a door turns it into an oracle for which codes are real. It also covers a booking code presented AFTER its own booking has ended, or for a booking that is no longer Booked: the AccessCode row outlives the slot by the grace window, and a door that distinguished 'spent' from 'never existed' would be that same oracle. 200, not 4xx: a refusal the firmware can act on must never look like an outage it should fall back from.

the club has suspended, rejected or not yet approved this member. Named rather than collapsed into not_recognised because a door has no LCD to explain itself and the distinction is what the desk needs from the audit row afterwards.

the scanner read a real, live ident code for a real user of this club who has NO membership row at all. Previously this opened the door: MembershipAccess tested 'the club recorded a decision and it was not approval', and about such a user it recorded none, so under active_member the door released for somebody the club has never admitted. Named rather than folded into member_not_active because the desk's next action differs — there is nothing to un-suspend, the person needs enrolling — and the door says neither out loud.

policy booking_window only: an active member with nothing booked inside [StartsAt - gate_early_entry_minutes, EndsAt]. Unreachable under the default active_member policy, which is why the policy is a tenant setting and this is a vector.

a BOOKING-ACTIVATION code presented before its own booking's entry window opens. A booking code is not a standing building key: under EVERY policy it opens a door only while now is inside [StartsAt - H, EndsAt] of the booking it names, where H is gate_early_entry_minutes under booking_window and max(gate_early_entry_minutes, roster_window_minutes + activation_cue_window_minutes) under active_member — the same horizon in which the member's own phone would show that code at all. Distinct from not_recognised because this one is worth telling a member apart from a dead code: they are early, not refused, and the door will open later. A sixty-second MemberIdent code never answers this — it names no booking.
anything but qr or code. A PIN against the whole membership roll is an oracle rather than an identification, and a door has no candidate set to check one against.

the MAC resolved to a CourtBox row. 200 with opened:false rather than a 404 or a 400, so a misconfigured board shows a refusal and stops rather than retrying an endpoint that will never answer it differently.

the gate's v3 settings, inside `gate` after unlock_seconds: power_restore_trust_minutes (tenant device_power_restore_trust_minutes, 0-120), net_fallback_minutes (device_net_fallback_minutes, 3-60) and ota_probation_minutes (device_ota_probation_minutes, 3-60). Sent only to a gate whose caps include ota:1, key:1 or net:1.

an OTA offer for the door_gate target: ota/cases.json image-gate's offer verbatim. The gate takes it only while the lock is engaged and no scan is waiting, streams it into the inactive app slot while hashing and feeding the watchdog, and switches the boot partition only after size, SHA-256 and the signature over the manifest all agree.
a key rotation in its grace window; the same object, and the same rules, as the court box's.
a network change; the same object, and the same all-or-nothing adoption, as the court box's.
